title: Diversity, equity & inclusion
summary: Fair opportunities, inclusive working relationships and software that considers the people using it.
lead: We value the different backgrounds, experiences and ways of thinking that people bring to our work. Our commitment is to treat people fairly and make participation possible.

sections.title: Our commitment
sections.body:
House Medical is committed to a professional environment in which people are treated with dignity, can contribute their ideas and are judged fairly on their work. This applies to our team, applicants, clients, suppliers and other people we work with.

We oppose unlawful discrimination, harassment, bullying and victimisation. Respectful disagreement can improve an idea; personal hostility and exclusion undermine the working environment.

sections.title: Fair access to opportunity
sections.body:
Our aim is to make recruitment, development and work opportunities accessible to people from a range of backgrounds. Decisions should be based on relevant skills, experience, potential and the needs of the role.

  • Use clear, relevant requirements when describing work and opportunities.
  • Consider how selection methods could disadvantage otherwise suitable people.
  • Discuss reasonable adjustments so that disabled people can participate in recruitment and work.
  • Support fair access to learning, feedback and progression.

sections.title: Inclusive decisions and everyday conduct
sections.body:
We aim to give people a meaningful opportunity to contribute to decisions that affect their work. That includes listening to different perspectives, explaining the reasons for decisions and avoiding assumptions about someone’s circumstances.

Inclusive working also means considering meeting formats, communication needs and the time people need to prepare. We encourage clear language and respectful feedback, especially when people have different technical backgrounds.

sections.title: Inclusion in the software we build
sections.body:
A person’s ability to complete a task should inform the design. Our design priorities include understandable language, clear instructions, keyboard access, readable content and useful feedback when something goes wrong.

Accessibility needs differ between products and users. We aim to identify those needs early and consider them throughout the work, alongside the relevant requirements for each product. We welcome feedback about barriers on this website.

sections.title: Suppliers and collaboration
sections.body:
We are open to working with a broad range of suppliers and partners, including smaller businesses and organisations led by underrepresented groups. Selection should consider suitability, quality, fairness and the needs of the work.

We expect professional, respectful behaviour in our working relationships and value collaboration between people with different disciplines and experiences.

sections.title: Raising a concern
sections.body:
If you experience or observe conduct that conflicts with this policy in your dealings with House Medical, contact us with enough information to understand the concern. Please avoid sending personal information about other people that is not needed.

Concerns should be considered fairly and sensitively. We oppose adverse treatment of anyone for raising a concern in good faith or helping to understand it.

title: Environment & sustainability
summary: Our 2030 net-zero ambition and priorities for considered purchasing, lower-impact working and less waste.
lead: Our environmental approach is to reduce avoidable impacts in the way we work, choose technology and use resources. The original ambition to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2030 remains our stated target.

sections.title: Our environmental ambition
sections.body:
House Medical’s ambition is to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2030 and to reduce its environmental footprint over time. This is a target, rather than a claim that our operations or products are already carbon neutral.

Meaningful progress depends on understanding the sources of emissions, making reductions and being clear about the scope and evidence behind any environmental claim. We do not treat the use of digital services alone as proof of a low environmental impact.

sections.title: Lower-impact working
sections.body:
We aim to limit avoidable energy use, material consumption and waste in our day-to-day work. Digital-first working can reduce printing and some journeys, while still carrying its own energy and equipment costs.

  • Use electronic documents where they are practical and accessible.
  • Switch off or reduce unnecessary equipment use.
  • Keep useful equipment in service where it remains secure and suitable.
  • Reuse, repair or responsibly recycle equipment and materials where possible.

sections.title: Thoughtful use of technology
sections.body:
Software choices have resource implications. Our priorities include avoiding unnecessary processing, limiting redundant data and choosing an appropriate level of technical complexity for the task.

For digital products, efficient interfaces and proportionate use of infrastructure are useful design considerations. Where AI or other intensive processing is proposed, its value should be considered alongside cost, energy use and simpler alternatives.

sections.title: Responsible purchasing and partners
sections.body:
We aim to consider environmental impact when choosing products, equipment and services. This includes suitability, expected life, repairability, waste and the information suppliers make available about their own practices.

We prefer to work with partners who take environmental responsibility seriously. Claims should be specific and supported by evidence; a label or general statement should not be the only basis for a decision.

sections.title: Travel and meetings
sections.body:
We aim to avoid journeys that can be replaced by an effective remote conversation. When travel is useful or necessary, we consider whether visits can be combined and whether a lower-emission transport option is practical.

The right approach depends on the purpose of the meeting, accessibility, the people involved and the quality of the work. Environmental considerations should inform that choice.

sections.title: Improvement and transparency
sections.body:
Our aim is to improve practical decisions over time and to be clear about what is an ambition, what action has been taken and what can be evidenced. This page does not publish a verified emissions baseline or quantified progress against the 2030 target.

Questions about this policy or the basis of an environmental claim can be sent to the studio. We welcome suggestions that could reduce avoidable impact in our work.

title: Health, safety & wellbeing
summary: A proactive approach to safe working, suitable workspaces, wellbeing and speaking up about risks.
lead: We are committed to supporting safe, healthy working conditions. This includes office work, remote working, travel and time spent in environments shared with clients and partners.

sections.title: Our approach to safe working
sections.body:
House Medical aims to identify foreseeable risks and take proportionate steps to reduce them. Health and safety should be considered when planning work, choosing equipment and changing working arrangements.

Everyone involved has a part to play: follow relevant instructions, use equipment appropriately and raise concerns promptly. A concern should be addressed before avoidable harm occurs.

sections.title: Workspaces and screen-based work
sections.body:
Much of software work involves sustained use of screens. Our priorities include suitable workstations, comfortable positioning, appropriate equipment and opportunities to vary activity.

  • Consider the desk, chair, screen, keyboard and surrounding working space together.
  • Identify discomfort, visual strain or other difficulties early.
  • Take suitable breaks or changes of activity during sustained screen work.
  • Keep workspaces free from avoidable electrical, fire and trip hazards.

Working from home does not remove the need to consider health and safety. Working arrangements should take account of the individual and the environment.

sections.title: Mental health and wellbeing
sections.body:
We recognise that workload, uncertainty and isolation can affect wellbeing as well as the quality of work. Our aim is to maintain realistic expectations, open communication and opportunities to raise difficulties.

Regular contact is particularly important when people work remotely. We encourage people to discuss pressures early and to consider sustainable working patterns, recovery time and the support appropriate to their circumstances.

sections.title: Visits, travel and shared environments
sections.body:
When working at a client or partner location, relevant site rules, induction arrangements and emergency procedures should be followed. People should know whom to contact if a problem occurs.

Travel and lone-working arrangements should consider the location, timing, task and means of keeping in contact. We prefer to work with organisations that also take the safety and wellbeing of people seriously.

sections.title: Concerns, incidents and learning
sections.body:
We encourage people to report hazards, incidents, near misses and work-related discomfort. Reporting provides an opportunity to understand what happened and improve the arrangements.

For a concern connected with House Medical, contact the studio and describe the relevant task or environment. In an immediate emergency, use the appropriate emergency service or the site’s emergency arrangements rather than waiting for an email response.

sections.title: Keeping the approach relevant
sections.body:
Risks can change when equipment, locations, roles or working patterns change. Our approach is to reconsider the arrangements when circumstances change and learn from concerns raised by the people doing the work.

This policy explains our general commitments. Specific activities may require additional instructions or assessments appropriate to the work.

title: Quality management
display_title:
Care in the detail.
Confidence in the result.
summary: Clear requirements, considered design, careful engineering and improvement informed by real use.
lead: Quality means that software helps people complete the right task, handles important details and can be understood and improved over time. Our commitment is to make those considerations part of the work.

sections.title: Start with a shared understanding
sections.body:
Our aim is to understand the purpose of the work, the people using it and the constraints that matter. Clear requirements and a shared view of a useful outcome provide the basis for sound decisions.

Important assumptions, dependencies and exclusions should be made visible. Where a question is unresolved, it should be identified rather than silently built into the product.

sections.title: Design for the complete task
sections.body:
Quality is reflected in the whole journey: what a person needs to know, the information they provide, the decisions they make and how they understand the result.

  • Use clear labels, instructions and relevant explanations.
  • Consider keyboard use, small screens and different access needs.
  • Make important actions and their consequences understandable.
  • Provide useful responses to missing information, errors and interrupted tasks.

sections.title: Engineering and risk awareness
sections.body:
Our engineering priorities include correctness, appropriate access, reliable handling of information and a structure that can be maintained. The level of assurance should reflect the consequences of something going wrong.

Calculations, validation rules, permissions, integrations and important edge cases deserve explicit attention. Relevant legal, contractual and product requirements should inform the decisions for each piece of work.

sections.title: Validation and release decisions
sections.body:
Before release, the intended behaviour should be checked against the requirements and the risks of the change. A successful demonstration of a typical journey is one part of that assessment.

Useful checks can also include invalid inputs, empty states, different screen sizes, keyboard access, integration failures and recovery paths. Known limitations should be visible when a release decision is made.

sections.title: Learning from use
sections.body:
Feedback, support requests and observed difficulties can reveal where a product needs attention. Our aim is to use that information to improve the details that affect people’s ability to complete their work.

Useful measures may include task completion, time and effort, recurring errors and the ease of recovering from a problem. Measures should be chosen for the product and supported by evidence before any performance claim is made.

sections.title: Suppliers, changes and accountability
sections.body:
Quality also depends on the services and components a product relies on. Suitability, reliability, support and the implications of a dependency should be considered alongside cost.

Changes should have a clear purpose, an understood impact and a proportionate way to check the outcome. This statement describes our quality commitments; it does not assert an independently certified management system.

title: Modern slavery & human rights
summary: Our zero-tolerance position on forced labour, human trafficking and exploitation in business relationships.
lead: House Medical has a zero-tolerance approach to modern slavery, forced labour and human trafficking. We are committed to acting ethically and with integrity in our dealings with other people and organisations.

sections.title: Our standing policy
sections.body:
Exploitation is unacceptable in our operations and supply chains. We will not knowingly support or do business with an organisation involved in forced labour, human trafficking or other forms of modern slavery.

This policy applies to our relationships with suppliers, contractors and business partners, regardless of their sector or location. We expect those organisations to uphold fair and humane labour practices in their own work.

sections.title: Where we need to remain aware
sections.body:
A software business depends on people, equipment and services. Relevant relationships can include technology and equipment suppliers, professional services, contractors and other organisations supporting the work.

We aim to consider the nature of a supplier’s activities and the information available about its practices. Risk should be assessed in context, including the use of recruitment agencies, subcontractors and extended supply chains.

sections.title: Expectations of suppliers and partners
sections.body:
• Work should be freely chosen, without coercion, threats or restriction of movement.
  • People should be treated with dignity and have fair, lawful terms of work.
  • Identity documents should not be withheld as a means of control.
  • Suppliers should take concerns about exploitation seriously and address them appropriately.
  • Business relationships should support lawful and ethical employment practices.

These expectations support our decisions about whom we work with. They do not amount to a guarantee about every activity in a supplier’s wider operations.

sections.title: Responding to a concern
sections.body:
We encourage people to raise a credible concern about exploitation connected with our operations or business relationships. Information should be handled sensitively and shared only as needed to understand and address the issue.

Appropriate action may include seeking further information, asking a supplier to address a concern, reconsidering the relationship or contacting the relevant authorities. The response should take account of the safety and interests of people who may be affected.

sections.title: How to contact us
sections.body:
Contact the studio if you have a concern relating to House Medical. Include the organisation or activity involved and the information that gives rise to your concern. Do not put yourself or another person at risk to obtain evidence.

If someone is in immediate danger, contact the appropriate emergency service. Emailing the studio is not an emergency reporting service.

sections.title: Scope of this statement
sections.body:
This is a standing policy statement of our commitments and expectations. It is not presented as a signed, board-approved annual statement for a specified financial year under section 54 of the Modern Slavery Act 2015.

Where an annual statutory statement is required, it needs to address the relevant reporting period, steps taken and approval requirements separately.

title: Data protection & privacy
summary: What this website processes, how we use correspondence, and how to ask about your personal information.
lead: This notice covers the public House Medical website at housemedical.co.uk and information you share when you contact the studio. Individual software products may have their own privacy notices and terms.

sections.title: Who is responsible
sections.body:
House Medical is the software studio of House Medical Consultants Ltd, company number 12540692. The company is responsible for the personal information it uses to manage enquiries and its business correspondence.

For a privacy question or request, email sales@housemedical.co.uk. You can also use the contact information on our company information page.

sections.title: Information we receive
sections.body:
If you email us, we receive your email address, your message and any attachments you choose to send. Correspondence may also contain your name, organisation, role or other details relevant to the conversation.

You choose what to share. We need enough information to understand and respond to an enquiry, but please avoid sending passwords, full financial records or personal information that is not needed for that first conversation.

Requests to the website can also generate technical information for the hosting provider, such as an IP address and information about the request. Our public website is hosted using GitHub Pages.

sections.title: Website features and local preferences
sections.body:
The website has no enquiry form, advertising trackers or third-party analytics scripts. Its fonts and visual assets are served with the website. The interactive signal field runs in your browser and does not submit the slider value or pointer movement to us.

If you change the motion setting, a preference is stored locally in your browser on that device. It is used to remember whether animations should run. You can change the setting on the site or remove it by clearing the site’s stored browser data.

The copy-email control writes the displayed address to your clipboard only when you select that action. Ordinary email links open your chosen email application.

sections.title: Why we use information
sections.body:
We use correspondence to understand and answer enquiries, discuss potential work, manage business relationships and keep relevant records.

  • Business correspondence: our legitimate interests in responding to people and managing the studio’s activities, taking account of their rights and expectations.
  • Contract discussions: taking steps at your request before entering a contract with you, or performing that contract, where this applies.
  • Required records: complying with legal obligations where particular information must be retained or provided.

We do not sell personal information or share correspondence with unrelated parties for their marketing. This website does not make automated decisions about visitors that have legal or similarly significant effects.

sections.title: Service providers and access
sections.body:
Hosting, email and IT service providers process information needed to operate their services. Relevant information may also need to be shared with professional advisers or authorities where this is necessary for the work or required by law.

Our commitment is to use appropriate safeguards, treat correspondence as confidential and limit access to people who need it for the relevant purpose. No internet or email service can eliminate every security risk.

Some providers may process information outside the UK. Where we arrange a restricted international transfer, appropriate safeguards must apply, such as an applicable adequacy arrangement or contractual protections. Contact us for information about arrangements relevant to your data.

sections.title: How long information is kept
sections.body:
Information should be kept only for as long as it is needed for the purpose for which it is used. Relevant considerations include whether an enquiry is still active, whether there is an ongoing working relationship, and whether records are needed for legal obligations or to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

A request to delete information will be considered in that context. If some information needs to be retained, we will explain the reason where we can. We do not promise immediate deletion where a relevant legal requirement or exemption applies.

sections.title: Your rights and requests
sections.body:
Depending on the circumstances, you may have rights to access your personal information, correct it, request erasure, restrict its use, object to processing or receive certain information in a portable form. The rights that apply depend on the purpose and lawful basis for the processing.

To make a request, email us and explain what you would like to know or do. We may need enough information to verify your identity and locate the relevant records. Please do not send identity documents unless they are requested through an appropriate process.

You can complain to the UK Information Commissioner’s Office if you are concerned about how your personal information is handled. See the ICO’s complaints information.

sections.title: Products and changes to this notice
sections.body:
A software product can process different information for a different purpose. Read its own privacy notice and terms before using it; this website notice does not replace product-specific information.

We may update this notice when the website or relevant arrangements change. The website edition date identifies the current published text. Material changes to the use of information should be explained to the people affected where required.
